requirements.evidence: All requirements are met. .env.example:1,7 sets APP_NAME=PegaFila and APP_LOCALE=pt_BR, and phpunit.xml:22-24 pins all three values. config/mail.php:16-21 sets 'theme' => 'pegafila', and pegafila.css:242-247 uses #0f7490 on .button-primary. lang/pt_BR.json:559,804 adds the 'Reset your password' and 'Verify your email address' subjects. routes/web.php:15-31 adds the five named routes, with guest middleware, throttle:6,1 on password.email, and auth+signed+throttle on verification.verify. PasswordResetLinkController.php:31-35 validates the e-mail and always returns back() with __('passwords.sent'). NewPasswordController.php:35-50 uses forceFill for the password and remember_token Str::random(60), fires PasswordReset and redirects to '/'. ResetPasswordRequest.php:30-32 has min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers() and confirmed. VerifyEmailController uses EmailVerificationRequest, which returns 403 on an id or hash mismatch, and redirects to '/'. reset-password.blade.php has a single e-mail input.

conventions.evidence: Mostly follows the conventions. Validation goes inline for the single field (PasswordResetLinkController.php:29) and through a Form Request for the three-field rule set (ResetPasswordRequest.php). The views use Bulma markup with {{ }} escaping, labels and aria attributes. CHANGELOG.md is updated under [Unreleased], and the new public methods have PHPDoc. Deviations: forgot-password.blade.php:1-17 and reset-password.blade.php:1-17 repeat the same <head> block (vite/CDN fallback) and page shell instead of sharing markup. They also hard-code a jsDelivr Bulma 0.9.4 CDN fallback that is not part of the project's asset pipeline.

security.evidence: No weakness found. The forgot-password response does not depend on whether the account exists (PasswordResetLinkController.php:33-35 ignores the broker status), and the endpoint is throttled. The reset validates the token through Password::reset and rotates remember_token. Verification relies on EmailVerificationRequest plus 'signed' and 'auth' middleware. All Blade output uses {{ }}, the token goes in a hidden input with escaping, and every form has @csrf. Changing the password via forceFill is appropriate and depends on the model's hashed cast, which the test at PasswordResetTest.php:1011 confirms.

tests.evidence: Coverage is thorough. AccountEmailsTest.php checks the rendered pt-BR subjects, greeting, button, body, translated sub-copy and the absence of English text, and confirms the brand colour is inlined on the button (line 869-872). AppLocaleTest.php checks the config pins, .env.example, the theme file and the lang entries. PasswordResetTest.php covers the form, the guest-only redirect, a known and an unknown address getting the same response, validation, the 429 throttle, the single e-mail input, the happy path (event, remember_token, redirect '/'), an invalid token, a token issued for another address, the password rules as a dataset, and the confirmation mismatch. VerifyEmailTest.php covers the happy path, an already-verified user, a wrong hash, a wrong id, a tampered URL, unsigned and expired links, and the throttle.

simplicity.evidence: The approach is direct: it reuses Laravel's notifications, the Password broker and EmailVerificationRequest. The weak spots are pegafila.css (297 lines), a full copy of the default theme that differs mainly in .button-primary colour, and the duplicated HTML shell in the two auth views.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are small, and the docblocks explain the anti-enumeration choice (PasswordResetLinkController.php:20-25). The tests are well named. Small nit: PasswordResetTest.php:926 declares a global const NEW_PASSWORD and VerifyEmailTest.php:1089 a global function signedVerificationUrl, both of which can clash with other Pest files.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: env and phpunit pins, mail config and theme, lang entries, routes, controllers and views from the contract, tests and CHANGELOG. Making User implement MustVerifyEmail (User.php:15) supports the verification feature. There is no login, registration, layouts, ui.php, Livewire or SCSS change.

issues.explanation: The theme is a full copy of Laravel's default theme with mostly only the primary button colour changed, so most of the 297 lines are vendor CSS the project now has to maintain.
Both views repeat the same HTML head and page shell, including a hard-coded jsDelivr Bulma 0.9.4 CDN fallback, instead of sharing markup.
A global const and a global helper function in Pest files can cause redeclaration errors if another test file defines the same names.

review.summary: The change adds the pt-BR account e-mails with a pegafila mail theme, the guest password-reset flow and the signed e-mail verification route, with config, lang, CHANGELOG and phpunit pins updated. It meets every requirement and contract item securely, including the non-enumerating response and the throttles, and ships thorough tests for the mails, validation, tampering and throttling. Only minor issues remain: a full copy of the default mail theme and a duplicated view shell, so it is approvable with nits.
